Main.sentence: Timothy Franz Geithner ( /ˈɡaɪtnər/ ; born August 18, 1961) is an American former ___E:central banker U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_bank)___ who served as the 75th ___E:United States secretary of the treasury U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_secretary_of_the_treasury)___ under President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ from 2009 to 2013. He was the ___E:President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_Federal_Reserve_Bank_of_New_York)___ of the ___E:Federal Reserve Bank of New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Reserve_Bank_of_New_York)___ from 2003 to 2009, following service in the ___E:Clinton administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Bill_Clinton)___ .

Since March 2014, he has served as president and chairman of ___E:Warburg Pincus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warburg_Pincus)___ , a ___E:private equity firm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_equity_firm)___ headquartered in New York City.

As President of the New York Fed and Secretary of the Treasury, Geithner had a key role in government efforts to recover from the ___E:2008 financial crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis)___ and the ___E:Great Recession U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Recession)___ .

At the New York Fed, Geithner helped manage crises involving ___E:Bear Stearns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bear_Stearns)___ , ___E:Lehman Brothers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehman_Brothers)___ , and the ___E:American International Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_International_Group)___ ; as Treasury Secretary, he oversaw allocation of $350 billion under the ___E:Troubled Asset Relief Program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troubled_Asset_Relief_Program)___ , enacted during the previous administration in response to the ___E:subprime mortgage crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subprime_mortgage_crisis)___ .

Geithner also managed the administration's efforts to restructure regulation of the nation's financial system,  attempts to spur recovery of the mortgage market and the automobile industry, demands for ___E:protectionism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protectionism)___ , tax reform, and negotiations with foreign governments on global finance issues.
Geithner was born in Manhattan, New York, to Peter Franz Geithner and Deborah Moore.

His father, a ___E:German American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_American)___ , was the director of the ___E:Ford Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Foundation)___ 's Asia program in New York during the 1990s, after working for the ___E:United States Agency for International Development U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Agency_for_International_Development)___ in Zambia and ___E:Zimbabwe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zimbabwe)___ .

During the early 1980s, Geithner's father oversaw the Ford Foundation's ___E:microfinance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microfinance)___ programs in Indonesia being developed by ___E:Ann Dunham Soetoro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Dunham_Soetoro)___ , Barack Obama's mother, and they met at least once in ___E:Jakarta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakarta)___ .

Geithner's paternal grandfather, Paul Herman Geithner (1902–1972), immigrated with his parents to the United States in 1908 from ___E:Zeulenroda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeulenroda-Triebes)___ , Germany.  [unreliable source?]

Geithner's mother, a ___E:Mayflower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayflower)___ descendant, belongs to a ___E:New England U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England)___ family.  [unreliable source?] Her father, Charles Frederick Moore, Jr., served as vice-president of public relations for the ___E:Ford Motor Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Motor_Company)___ from 1952 to 1964, and advised President ___E:Dwight D. Eisenhower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower)___ , as well as ___E:Nelson Rockefeller U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Rockefeller)___ and ___E:George W. Romney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Romney)___ , on their respective presidential campaigns.

His uncle, ___E:Jonathan Moore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Moore_(State_Department_official))___ , served in the departments of ___E:Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense)___ , ___E:Justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice)___ and ___E:State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State)___ , as well as in the United Nations.

Geithner spent most of his childhood living abroad, including in Zimbabwe; Zambia; India; and Thailand, where he completed high school at the ___E:International School Bangkok U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_School_Bangkok)___ .

He studied ___E:Mandarin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_Chinese)___ at ___E:Peking University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peking_University)___ in 1981, and at ___E:Beijing Normal University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing_Normal_University)___ in 1982.  Like his father, paternal grandfather and uncle; Geithner attended ___E:Dartmouth College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dartmouth_College)___ , graduating in 1983, with an A.B. in Government and ___E:Asian studies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_studies)___ ,  then earned a M.A. in international economics and East Asian studies from ___E:Johns Hopkins University's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University)___ ___E:School of Advanced International Studies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_H._Nitze_School_of_Advanced_International_Studies)___ , in 1985.   He has also studied Japanese.

Geithner worked for ___E:Kissinger Associates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kissinger_Associates)___ in Washington, D.C., from 1985 to 1988, when he joined the International Affairs division of the ___E:U.S. Treasury Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_the_Treasury)___ .

He served as an ___E:attaché U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attach%C3%A9)___ at the ___E:Embassy of the United States in Tokyo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embassy_of_the_United_States_in_Tokyo)___ , then as deputy assistant secretary for international ___E:monetary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monetary_policy)___ and ___E:financial policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiscal_policy)___ (1995–1996), senior deputy assistant secretary for international affairs (1996–1997), and assistant secretary for international affairs (1997–1998).

He was ___E:Under Secretary of the Treasury for International Affairs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Secretary_of_the_Treasury_for_International_Affairs)___ (1998–2001) under Secretaries ___E:Robert Rubin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Rubin)___ and ___E:Lawrence Summers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Summers)___ ,  who are widely considered to have been his mentors.
While at the Treasury Department, he helped manage financial crises in Brazil, Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea, and Thailand.

In 2001, Geithner left the Treasury to join the ___E:Council on Foreign Relations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_on_Foreign_Relations)___ as a Senior Fellow in the International Economics department.
He was director of the Policy Development and Review Department at the ___E:International Monetary Fund U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund)___ from 2001 to 2003.
In October 2003, Geithner was named president of the ___E:Federal Reserve Bank of New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Reserve_Bank_of_New_York)___ .
As president of the New York Fed, he served as Vice Chairman of the ___E:Federal Open Market Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Open_Market_Committee)___ .

In 2006, he became a member of the ___E:Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C.)___ -based financial advisory body, the ___E:Group of Thirty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_of_Thirty)___ .

In 2005, Geithner expressed concern over Wall Street trading in ___E:financial derivatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derivative_(finance))___ , which ultimately contributed to the spread of the ___E:2008 financial crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis)___ , though he did not pursue major reforms.

In 2004, Geithner called on banks to "build a sufficient cushion against adversity", though in May 2007, he expressed support for the ___E:Basel II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basel_II)___ accord, which critics, including ___E:Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Deposit_Insurance_Corporation)___ chairperson ___E:Sheila Bair U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheila_Bair)___ , argued would reduce the amount of capital banks would be required to hold to guard against losses.

That month, in a speech at the ___E:Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Reserve_Bank_of_Atlanta)___ , Geithner stated, "Financial innovation has improved the capacity to measure and manage risk," but also cautioned that "financial innovation and global financial integration do not offer the prospect of eliminating the risk of asset price and ___E:credit cycles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credit_cycle)___ , of manias and panics, or of shocks that could have systemic consequences."
As president of the New York Fed, Geithner was a central figure in the U.S. government's response to the ___E:2008 financial crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis)___ .

In mid-March 2008, together with then-Treasury Secretary ___E:Henry Paulson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Paulson)___ , Geithner arranged the rescue and ___E:fire sale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire_sale)___ of ___E:Bear Stearns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bear_Stearns)___ , which was at risk of bankruptcy, to ___E:JPMorgan Chase U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JPMorgan_Chase)___ for $2 per share (later raised to $10 per share  ).
The Fed agreed to provide financing for the deal and support up to $30 billion of Bear Stearns's "less-liquid assets", despite some internal protests.

In doing so, the New York Fed allowed Bear Stearns itself to calculate the value of assets acquired by the government and exposed itself to losses should those assets have declined in value, though JPMorgan agreed to absorb the first $1 billion in losses.

The New York Fed stored these assets in the ___E:Maiden Lane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maiden_Lane_Transactions)___ ___E:limited liability company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limited_liability_company)___ and awarded ___E:no-bid contracts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No-bid_contract)___ to the Wall Street ___E:asset manager U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asset_management)___ ___E:BlackRock U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BlackRock)___ for management of the assets, with the intent of ridding itself of the assets within 10 years.

In testimony before the ___E:Senate Banking Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Banking,_Housing,_and_Urban_Affairs)___ , countering concerns that the rescue would invite ___E:moral hazard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moral_hazard)___ problems, Geithner argued that "a sudden, disorderly failure of Bear would have brought with it unpredictable but severe consequences for the functioning of the broader financial system and the broader economy."  Under questioning from Senator ___E:Chris Dodd U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Dodd)___ , Geithner denied involvement in setting the share price of JPMorgan's purchase of Bear Stearns.

Bear Stearns and JPMorgan chief executives ___E:Alan Schwartz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Schwartz)___ and ___E:Jamie Dimon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_Dimon)___ testified that Geithner and ___E:Federal Reserve Chairman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chair_of_the_Federal_Reserve)___ ___E:Ben Bernanke U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Bernanke)___ were aware of the amount being discussed and encouraged negotiators to keep the price low to avoid rewarding investors.
In the late summer of 2008, troubles at the financial services firm ___E:Lehman Brothers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehman_Brothers)___ were accelerating.

In late August, the company announced that 1,500 employees (6% of its workforce) would be laid off, following 6,000 layoffs since June 2007.  On September 9, Lehman's share price plunged 45% on fears that the company was facing billions of dollars in losses, and on news that a potential investment in the company by ___E:Korea Development Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korea_Development_Bank)___ had fallen through.

Three days later, Geithner convened a meeting of Wall Street executives, Secretary Paulson, and ___E:Securities and Exchange Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Securities_and_Exchange_Commission)___ Chairman ___E:Christopher Cox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Cox)___ to review exposure to Lehman's fortunes and discuss a possible liquidation of Lehman.

Geithner indicated that the government would not save Lehman and urged the executives to cooperate on an industry solution, warning that the crisis could spread to their own firms should a deal not be reached.

Government officials believed Lehman's collapse would be less dangerous than that of Bear Stearns,  though Geithner sought to avoid that contingency nonetheless, citing the increase in market fragility by the time of Lehman's crisis.

Nevertheless, no industry rescue materialized. ___E:Bank of America U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_America)___ , which had been in talks to purchase Lehman, pulled out after the government indicated it would not take on Lehman's risky real-estate assets, as it had with Bear Stearns.

On September 15, Lehman announced that it would ___E:file for bankruptcy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bankruptcy_of_Lehman_Brothers)___ , making it the largest investment bank failure since ___E:Drexel Burnham Lambert U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drexel_Burnham_Lambert)___ in 1990.

Geithner, Paulson, and Bernanke later argued that Lehman's financial situation was too dire for the government to have legally rescued it.  A team from ___E:Goldman Sachs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldman_Sachs)___ and ___E:Credit Suisse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credit_Suisse)___ had estimated prior to Lehman's bankruptcy filing that Lehman's liabilities exceeded its assets by tens of billions of dollars (i.e., a negative ___E:net worth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Net_worth)___ ).
Geithner was instrumental in government dealings with the ___E:American International Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_International_Group)___ (AIG) insurance company.

Over the summer of 2008, as ___E:credit rating agencies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credit_rating_agency)___ downgraded ___E:mortgage-backed securities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortgage-backed_security)___ , AIG faced mounting demands to provide increased collateral to buyers of its ___E:credit default swaps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credit_default_swap)___ .
Consequently, by the time of Lehman's failure in September, AIG was facing a rapidly increasing multibillion-dollar capital shortfall.

On September 13, AIG chief ___E:Robert B. Willumstad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_B._Willumstad)___ informed Geithner that the company would need to raise $40 billion and asked for government assistance in doing so. Geithner rejected the request for government funds and pressed AIG to find a private-sector solution to the company's ___E:liquidity crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquidity_crisis)___ .
On the morning of September, Geithner reiterated this decision at a meeting of Wall Street executives and requested that Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan organize an industry-based solution.
By that evening, private-sector appetite for an AIG rescue has dissipated.

Later that night, a consensus emerged at the New York Fed that AIG, with $500 billion in troubled credit-swap obligations, could not be allowed to fail. At a meeting of the Federal Reserve in Washington the next day, Geithner and Paulson proposed lending $85 billion to AIG, with all of AIG's assets held as collateral, in exchange for a 79.9% ___E:equity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equity_(finance))___ stake in AIG and veto rights over dividend payments.
Upon delivering this offer to AIG, Geithner informed Willumstad that there would be "no negotiation".

As a result of Lehman Brothers's failure, ___E:money market funds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money_market_fund)___ with exposure to Lehman securities found themselves in distress on the day of Lehman's bankruptcy filing.
One such fund was the ___E:Reserve Primary Fund U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_Primary_Fund)___ .

Due to the highly stable ___E:net asset value U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Net_asset_value)___ (NAV) of money market funds ($1.00 per share), money market funds were extensively relied on by companies for regular cash demands (e.g., payroll).

Following Lehman's bankruptcy filing, due to a slowdown in credit markets, the Primary Fund was unable to sell once ___E:liquid assets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_liquidity)___ to meet rapidly mounting demands for the redemption of investments.
Geithner's New York Fed had been informed of the worsening situation at 7:50 that morning, and the next day rebuffed a request from the Primary Fund to assist it in making payments.

Unable to sell Lehman's securities held by the fund, the board of the Primary Fund announced that it would freeze redemptions for seven days and reduce its NAV to $0.97 per share, meaning a money market fund would ___E:break the buck U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Money_market_fund#Breaking_the_buck)___ for only the second time in the industry's history.

To stabilize the financial market, Geithner proposed that the traditional ___E:investment banks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investment_bank)___ Goldman Sachs and ___E:Morgan Stanley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Stanley)___ transform themselves into ___E:bank holding companies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_holding_company)___ to ensure continuing access to funding.
Both banks completed the restructuring by September 21.
Geithner believed, along with Paulson, that the Treasury needed new authority to respond to the ___E:2008 financial crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis)___ .
Paulson described Geithner as a "very unusually talented young man...[who] understands government and understands markets".

During the ___E:2008 presidential campaign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_US_Presidential_election)___ , Geithner was rumored to be a possible choice for Treasury Secretary for both ___E:John McCain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain)___ and ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ .

On November 24, 2008, ___E:President-elect U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President-elect_of_the_United_States)___ ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ announced his intention to nominate Geithner to be Treasury Secretary.

During his confirmation, it was disclosed that Geithner had not paid $35,000 in ___E:Social Security and Medicare payroll taxes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Insurance_Contributions_Act_tax)___ from 2001 through 2004 while working for the ___E:International Monetary Fund U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund)___ .
The IMF, as an international agency, did not withhold payroll taxes, but instead reimbursed the usual employer responsibility of these taxes to employees.

Geithner received the reimbursements and paid the amounts received to the government, but had not paid the remaining half which would normally have been withheld from his pay. The issue, as well as other errors relating to past deductions and expenses, were noted during a 2006 audit by the ___E:Internal Revenue Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_Revenue_Service)___ .

Geithner subsequently paid the additional taxes owed.   In a statement to the ___E:Senate Finance Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_Finance_Committee)___ , Geithner called the tax issues "careless", "avoidable", and "unintentional" errors.
Geithner testified that he used the software ___E:TurboTax U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TurboTax)___ to prepare his 2001 and 2002 returns, but that the tax errors were his own responsibility.

On January 26, 2009, the ___E:U.S. Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ confirmed Geithner's appointment by a vote of 60–34.   Geithner was sworn in as Treasury Secretary by Vice President ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ and witnessed by President Barack Obama.

Geithner had authority over the second ___E:tranche U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranche)___ of $350 billion from the $700 billion banking ___E:bailout bill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_Economic_Stabilization_Act_of_2008)___ passed by Congress in October 2008. Under the Financial Stability Plan, he proposed to create a new investment fund to provide a market for the legacy loans and securities—the so-called " ___E:toxic assets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toxic_asset)___ "—burdening the financial system, using a mix of taxpayer and private money.
He also proposed expanding a lending program that would spend as much as $1 trillion to cover the decline in the issuance of securities backed by consumer loans.

He further proposed to give banks new infusions of capital with which to lend. In exchange, banks would be required to cut the ___E:salaries and perks of executives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_compensation)___ and sharply limit ___E:dividends U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dividends)___ and ___E:corporate acquisitions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mergers_and_acquisitions)___ .

The plan was criticized by ___E:Nobel laureates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Memorial_Prize_in_Economic_Sciences)___ ___E:Paul Krugman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Krugman)___ and ___E:Joseph Stiglitz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Stiglitz)___ , a former ___E:World Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank)___ ___E:Chief Economist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank_Chief_Economist)___ .

The ___E:Troubled Asset Relief Program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troubled_Asset_Relief_Program)___ (TARP) and ___E:takeover U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_policies_and_the_subprime_mortgage_crisis#Federal_takeover_of_Fannie_Mae_and_Freddie_Mac)___ of ___E:Fannie Mae U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fannie_Mae)___ and ___E:Freddie Mac U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Mac)___ amounted a combined outflow of $620.3 billion in Treasury funds in the form of spending, investments, and loans.
As of July 2016, $689 billion has been returned to the Treasury, primarily in the form of refunds provided by bailed-out companies and revenue from dividends.

Although President Obama expressed strong support for Geithner, outrage over hundreds of millions of dollars in ___E:bonus payments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonus_payment)___ (or ___E:employee "retention" U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Employee_retention)___ payments) by the ___E:American International Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_International_Group)___ , which had received more than $170 billion in federal bailout aid, undermined public support in early 2009. In March 2009, AIG paid $165 million in bonuses to its financial products division, the unit responsible for the company's ___E:near collapse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_International_Group#2008_liquidity_crisis_and_government_bailout)___ the year prior, following $55 million paid to the same division in December 2008 and $121 million in bonus payments to senior executives.

In early November 2008, a joint committee of the ___E:Federal Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Reserve_System)___ , ___E:Ernst & Young U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_%26_Young)___ , and AIG concluded that the bonus payments, which were in contracts predating the government takeover, could not be legally stopped.

During his time at the New York Fed and early in his tenure as Treasury Secretary, Geithner's aides had closely dealt with AIG on compensation issues, though Geithner indicated he was not aware of AIG's plans for bonus payments until March 10, 2009. On March 11, 2009, Geithner called ___E:Ed Liddy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Liddy)___ , the AIG chief, to protest the bonus payouts and request that the contracting containing the bonuses be renegotiated.
Later in March, Liddy requested that employees who received bonuses of more than $100,000 return half of the payment.
At Geithner's urging, Liddy cut $9.6 million in payments to company's top 50 executives in half and tied the remainder to performance.

In November 2009, ___E:Neil Barofsky U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Barofsky)___ , the Treasury Department Inspector General responsible for oversight of TARP funds, issued a report critical of the use of $62.1 billion of government funds to redeem derivative contracts held by several large banks which AIG had insured against losses.
The banks received face value for the contracts although their market value at the time was much lower.
In the report, Barofsky said the payments "provided [the banks] with tens of billions of dollars they likely would have not otherwise received".
Terms for use of the funds had been negotiated with the ___E:New York Federal Reserve Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Reserve_Bank_of_New_York)___ while Geithner was president.

In January 2010, Rep. ___E:Darrell Issa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darrell_Issa)___ released a series of e-mails between AIG and the New York Fed. In these e-mails, the Fed urged AIG not to disclose the full details of the payments publicly or in its ___E:SEC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Securities_and_Exchange_Commission)___ filings.
Issa pushed for an investigation of the matter, and for records and e-mails from the Fed to be subpoenaed.

Rep. ___E:Edolphus Towns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edolphus_Towns)___ , Chairman of the ___E:House Oversight and Government Reform Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Oversight_and_Government_Reform)___ , issued subpoenas for the records and scheduled hearings for late January. ___E:Federal Reserve Chairman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chair_of_the_Federal_Reserve)___ ___E:Ben Bernanke U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Bernanke)___ said the Fed would welcome a full review of its actions regarding the AIG payments.

Geithner and his predecessor, former Treasury Secretary ___E:Henry Paulson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Paulson)___ , both appeared before the Committee on January 27. Geithner defended the bailout of AIG and the payments to the banks, while reiterating previous denials of any involvement in efforts to withhold details of the transactions.
His testimony was met with skepticism and angry disagreement by House members of both parties.

In his book Bailout: How Washington Abandoned Main Street While Rescuing Wall Street , ___E:Neil Barofsky U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Barofsky)___ argues that Geithner never had the intention to utilize the ___E:Home Affordable Modification Program U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Affordable_Modification_Program)___ as intended by Congress.
Instead of providing relief for homeowners to avoid foreclosures, it was Geithner's plan that the bank should proceed with these foreclosures.

Geithner said that he "estimates" that the banks "can handle ten million foreclosures, over time", and that HAMP "will help foam the runway for them" by “keeping the full flush of foreclosures from hitting the financial system all at the same time."  As such, "banks participating in the program have rejected four million borrowers’ requests for help, or 72 percent of their applications, since the process began".  ___E:Citimortgage U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citigroup)___ and ___E:JPMorgan Chase U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JPMorgan_Chase)___ were among the banks that refused the most HAMP claims.
As such, the program only helped 887,001 people out of the over 4 Million people that were originally estimated to be able to benefit from the program.

In written comments to the Senate Finance Committee during his confirmation hearings, Geithner stated that the new administration believed ___E:China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_Republic_of_China)___ was "manipulating" ___E:its currency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renminbi)___ and that the Obama administration would act "aggressively" using "all the diplomatic avenues" to change China's currency practices.

The Obama administration would pressure China diplomatically to change this practice more strongly than the ___E:George W. Bush Administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush_Administration)___ had done.  The United States maintained that China's actions hurt American businesses and contributed to the ___E:2008 financial crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_financial_crisis)___ .
Shortly after assuming his role as Secretary of the Treasury, Geithner met in Washington with Chinese Foreign Minister ___E:Yang Jiechi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yang_Jiechi)___ .

He furthered that China was acting "very, very aggressive in a strategy they started several decades ago", which he defined as the ultimatum of transferring technology or being unable to produce products in China.

'I believe there is no credible argument to be made that the purpose of government is to borrow from future generations of Americans to finance an extension of tax cuts for the top 2 percent,' [he] said in a recent speech."

Geithner was Obama's lead negotiator about the ___E:fiscal cliff U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_fiscal_cliff)___ and the increase in the 2013 ___E:debt limit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debt_limit)___ .

For example, on December 5, 2012, Geithner confirmed leaks from the White House,   Treasury Secretary Geithner told CNBC that the Obama Administration is "absolutely" willing to go over the fiscal cliff if Republicans refused to back off from their opposition to raising rates on wealthier Americans.
